relationships.subject: cyclovirobuxine D
relationships.evidence_quote: Dose-response relationship of CVB-D inhibition of Cav3.2 peak current obtained at a HP of −100 mV yields an IC50 of 2.28 ± 0.35 μM (Figures 3C,D).

relationships.subject: cyclovirobuxine D
relationships.evidence_quote: CVB-D dose-dependently inhibited Cav2.2 expressed in HEK 293T cells, with an IC50 value of 1.82 ± 1.40 μM (Figures 3E–H).

relationships.subject: cyclovirobuxine D
relationships.evidence_quote: These results indicate that CVB-D potently inhibits native Cav3.2 and Cav2.2 channels and that inhibition of Cav3.2, but not Cav2.2, greatly decreases the excitability of DRG neurons.

relationships.subject: cyclovirobuxine D
relationships.evidence_quote: and had negligible effect on pain-related Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 voltage-gated Na+ channels (Figures 2H,I)

relationships.subject: cyclovirobuxine D
relationships.evidence_quote: and did not affect agonist-induced currents in HEK 293T cells expressing TRPM8 and TRPV1

key_findings: Cyclovirobuxine D relieves carrageenan, CFA and paclitaxel-induced hypersensitivity in mice, comparable to Z944.
CVB-D inhibits Cav3.2 (IC50 2.28 uM) and Cav2.2 but not Nav1.7, Nav1.8 or TRPV1; Cav3.2 inhibition dominates its analgesia and reduction of DRG excitability.
